info.name: Strava (aifitnessapi.com)
info.description: Strava: OAuth 2.0 and Webhook samples requests built from the vendor documentation aifitnessapi.com quotes. Generated by scripts/build-collections.mjs; no secrets included. https://aifitnessapi.com/collections

item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Strava's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/strava-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize. Authorization URL for web apps. Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Strava redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Scope: Required. Comma- or space-delimited; this tool uses commas. The athlete can untick any requested scope, so check the scope the redirect returns. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Documented scopes (joined with commas):
- read: Public segments, public routes, public profile data, public posts, public events, club feeds, and leaderboards
- read_all: Private routes, private segments, and private events for the user
- profile:read_all: All profile information, even if the user set profile visibility to Followers or Only You
- profile:write: Update the user's weight and Functional Threshold Power (FTP), and star or unstar segments
- activity:read: Activities visible to Everyone and Followers, excluding privacy zone data; required for activity webhooks
- activity:read_all: As activity:read, plus privacy zone data and Only You activities
- activity:write: Create manual activities and uploads, and edit activities visible to the app

PKCE: Not mentioned on Strava's Authentication page.

Also documented: https://www.strava.com/oauth/mobile/authorize. Mobile apps (Android intent or iOS) use the mobile authorize endpoint; the Strava app opens if installed. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

https://www.strava.com/oauth/token. Token URL, with the client ID and secret, for both the code exchange and refresh. (Strava's own curl samples post to https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token.)

Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Client credentials go in the form body.

Token lifetime: Six hours from creation. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Note: The authorization code is short-lived and single-use. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Note: approval_prompt is auto by default; force always shows the prompt. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Note: localhost and 127.0.0.1 are allowed as redirect hosts. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Note: Deauthorize with POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/revoke (HTTP Basic, the token in the body), the only supported endpoint from June 1, 2027. Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

Refresh: Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. If the current access token expires in more than an hour, the same one comes back; once a new refresh token is returned the old one stops working.

Source: Strava Developers, “Authentication”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/authentication/

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Strava's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: No signature is documented for event POSTs. Subscription validation is a GET with hub.mode, hub.challenge and hub.verify_token; echo hub.challenge as JSON. Source: Strava Developers, “Webhook Events API”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/webhooks/

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Strava prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: Acknowledge each POST with 200 OK within two seconds; do further work asynchronously.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#strava.

request.description:
Sent when an activity is created or deleted, when its title, type or privacy changes, and when an athlete revokes access (updates then holds "authorized": "false").

Strava's example event (Example Request). Source: Strava Developers, “Webhook Events API”, https://developers.strava.com/docs/webhooks/

variable.description: Your app's client ID, from the vendor's developer console.
Keep it in a Postman or Bruno environment marked secret. This collection ships it empty.
The redirect URI registered with the vendor.
Scopes to request, joined as the vendor documents (see the authorization request).
A random value you check on the redirect.
The refresh_token from the token response.
